newsitem.title: USA: TRW gets approval to build satellite.
newsitem.headline: TRW gets approval to build satellite.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Communications Commission has given TRW Inc final approval to build and operate the Odyssey global, satellite-based cell phone system, the company said.
TRW said the approval followed the commission's recent adoption of a frequency band allocation plan that made space available for use by satellite feeder links and other radio systems.
Odyssey's links between satellites and Earth stations use the newly designated spectrum, and TRW's license for those links had been conditional pending completion of the commission's plan, it said.
"Odyssey is moving ahead to obtain licenses in other countries," it said.

The company said Odyssey is a proposed personal communications satellite services system that will allow subscribers equipped with only a pocket telephone to reach any phone on Earth, from anywhere on the planet.
Service, which is scheduled to begin in 2001, would also provide fax, computer data, and short message services, it added.
The company said Odyssey Telecommunications International Inc, which has TRW Inc and Teleglobe Inc as founding shareholders, is developing the patented Odyssey system.
